description.narrative: The additional financing will expand the scope and reinforce the outcome and outputs of the ongoing National Disaster Risk Management Project. This will be achieved by supporting persons displaced by disasters and enhancing the executing agency’s technical and institutional capacities for strategic disaster risk management (DRM). The overall project will further enhance the disaster preparedness of the country against the projected heightened exposure to climate change.

Reports and Recommendations of the President
Grant 0614: 100% of contracts awarded and 100% disbursed as of 20 Jun 2025
Grant 0865: 63% of contracts awarded and 24% disbursed as of 20 Jun 2025

Progress Toward Outcome: On 4 Oct 2022, ADB approved the minor change in project scope to include additional consulting services to undertake advanced feasibility designs for the Additional Financing to the project and Direct contracting of the existing project implementation consultant (through amendment to the existing contract.
Some results are in the Audited Project Financial Statements | Jun 2024: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/52106/52106-001-apfs-en_3.pdf
Some results are in the Safeguards Due Diligence Reports | Apr 2025: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/52106/52106-001-sddr-en_0.pdf
Some results are in the Social Monitoring Reports | Mar 2025: https://www.adb.org/sites/default/files/project-documents/52106/52106-001-smr-en_0.pdf

Status of Implementation Progress: Completed. The nine-year investment plan and an options paper on funding opportunities to support the investment plan as a road map for funding, were completed in June 2022. The investment plan is supported by an economic analysis for each of the four regions of Tajikistan. The principal investments with respect to natural hazards risk mitigation are improvements to the regional transportation corridors, earthquake resilient structures, flood protection, and reforestation initiatives. Soft investment in CBDRM and awareness raising are proposed cornerstone investments for natural hazards risk mitigation. The review of the nine-year investment plan was submitted in July 2022 to incorporate suggested methodology, if aligned with methodology stipulated in the TOR and approved during the inception report. A comprehensive report on funding opportunities to support the investment plan, as a guide for securing financing was finalized. The financing mechanisms included public funding, targeted local public funding, counterpart funding, and the establishment of a Trust Fund. The EA is in the process of engaging with the Ministry of Finance, sector ministries/agencies, higher government authorities, and development partners. The objective is to propose an approach that development partner agencies could utilize to allocate funding to Disaster Risk Reduction programs, projects, and activities in Tajikistan. Completed. The EA and Project Implementation Consultant (PIC) established official Technical Working Groups (TWG) within each ministry or agency and cultivated partnership with development partners. The tasks included a comprehensive review of DRM policies, national strategies, and institutional provisioning documents, as well as conducting an in-depth institutional functional survey of seven sectors and eight departments of CESCD. This also entailed the formulation of a vision and mission statement and objectives for CESCD, determining the role of CESCD within the realm of DRM, outlining departmental functions, analyzing the inter-agency linkages for CESCD's business process model, and proposing three options for the reorganizing of CESCD institutionally. The activities under Sub-output 1 were completed by the PIC as of December 2021 and the EA has accepted the deliverable. The CESCD institutional plan, which includes capacity-building initiatives for gender-responsive Disaster Risk Management implemented (DRM). The CESCD has confirmed on 22 July 2024 and provided supporting documents on 24 May 2024. Completed. This output indicator was contingent upon the outputs derived from output indicators 1a, 1d, 1c, and training plan implemented. The PIC reviewed the pre-existing organizational structures, operational management systems, and the delineation of roles and responsibilities within various departments, divisions, and units of the CESCD. Subsequently, the CESCD reached a consensus on its DRM vision, mission, and a set of objectives. In June 2021, the PIC presented the final Five-Year Business Operational Plan (2021-2025) for the CESCD which encompassed the identification of research and data requirements, as well as established implementation targets and project outcomes. The deliverable has been completed. Completed. The PIC, in collaboration with the designated focal points representing the seven sector ministries/agencies, successfully incorporated DRM, climate change, gender equality, and social inclusion issues in sectoral strategies of the following entities: the Ministry of Health and Social Protection, the Ministry of Education and Science, the Ministry of Transport, and the State Management Committee for Land Management and Geodesy. In addition, these considerations have been mainstreamed into the draft Mid-term Development Program of the Republic of Tajikistan for 2021-2025, and the Adaptation section of the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC) for Tajikistan. The final deliverable was duly submitted by June 2021, and the EA has officially accepted the deliverable. Substantially achieved. The PIC finalized the production of legal briefs and conducted an extensive detailed legal review of the country's legal framework pertaining to Climate Change and Disaster Risk Management (CCDRM). In response to the CESCD's request, the PIC also authored a comments paper concerning the draft Law on Civil Protection, incorporating findings and recommendations based on a comparative analysis against international standards and good practice. The integration of gender equality and social inclusion consideration into national legal instruments and sector-specific laws pertaining to the CCDRM was diligently addressed. Furthermore, the PIC was tasked by the CESCD to formulate an options paper aimed at strengthening the national DRM Law which also included the development of provisions related to climate change, gender equality and social inclusion, vulnerable groups, and international assistance. The activities were successfully concluded by January 2021, and the deliverable has been accepted by the EA. The CESCD has confirmed on 22 July 2024 and provided the supporting documents on 24 May 2024.The project effectiveness was only declared on 14 March 2023. Completed. The Multi-hazard risk profiles for the Gorno-Badakhshan Autonomous Oblast (GBAO), Sughd, Regions of Republican Subordination (RRS), and Khatlon regions were prepared by October 2022; underwent a final review from a climate change and gender perspective; and were submitted to the CESCD on 26 October 2023 for their review and acceptance. The CESCD has reviewed the four profiles and find them to satisfy their requirements. The profiles are written in a style that enables the CESCD to develop and promote risk reduction programs that are specific to the hazards of each of the four regions. The profiles also link directly to the link to the risk reduction measures presented in the Nine-year Investment Plan. The CESCD has accepted the four Regional Multi-hazard Risk Profiles. Completed. The contract to develop and implement the DMIS was awarded to the Integrated Project Services LLP, based in Kazakhstan, for the sum of $197,000.00; and completed on 28 September 2023. The CESCD confirmed to ADB that they have received the DMIS Version 1.0 and that the DMIS is operational. The EA has acknowledged and accepted the deliverable. Completed. The Doppler Weather Radar, which was a new installation, became operational in August 2021; and the monitoring and early warning system (EWS) for the Sarez Lake was commissioned in September 2021. In November 2022, ADB granted approval for the procurement of the (i) EWS equipment for the CESCD; and (ii) replacement parts and batteries for existing EWS mobile communications equipment. The Quotation Evaluation Reports (QERs) were approved on 24 January 2023; and the contracts were awarded to AT Communication International LLC (Georgia) in the amounts of $83,982 and $79,170, respectively. The contracts were successfully completed on 4 May 2023. The CESCD's EWS communication system was improved by incorporating the additional pieces of equipment. The PIC provided a concept paper regarding the design of a national EWS and a conceptual design of multi-hazard early warning system (MHEWS) on 6 November 2023 for review and acceptance by the CESCD. The MHEWS conceptual report and the MHEWS Remote Sensing and Services report were reviewed by the CESCD and found them satisfying their requirements. Both reports will support the CESCD in presenting and developing a responsive national EWS approach in collaboration with other line ministries through the National Platform for Disaster Risk Reduction. The CESCD has accepted the Multi-hazard Early Warning System reports. Completed. The Aga Khan Agency for Habitat (AKAH) conducted a kick-off session regarding the CBDRM program in May 2022. The CBDRM program was conducted within the high-risk districts and villages to achieve the objectives of the CBDRM. The AKAH implemented the CBDRM program in 63 villages, covering 29 high risk districts in all four regions of Tajikistan. The program reached 1,869 community members, of whom 1,035 (55%) were women. Women participation ranged from 7% to 73% when disaggregated by individual villages. The CESCD has verified the accomplishment of this sub-output and has considered the task as successfully completed. Completed. The National DRM plan was completed, and a stakeholder consultation workshop was held on 10 November 2023. The National DRM plan was finalized and submitted to the CESCD on 30 November 2023. The disaster risk management plan will support sector strategies and CESCD's input to the National Platform for Disaster Risk Reduction. The CESCD has reviewed the National DRM Plan and found that it satisfied the CESCD's request to produce a DRM plan that is strategic and will support the development of responsive sector strategies by the line ministries and CESCD's input to the National Platform for Disaster Risk Reduction. The CESCD has accepted the National Disaster Risk Management Plan. Completed. The installation of the Sarez Lake monitoring and EWS was successfully completed with the official handover in December 2021, marking the fulfillment of this deliverable. The contract was awarded in the amount of $750,000 on 6 November 2020 and was completed on 7 September 2021. The CESCD has confirmed the ongoing operational functioning of the system as of November 2023. The project effectiveness was only declared on 14 March 2023.
